Bereaved

buh-REEVD -- from Old English be- (an intensifying prefix) + reafian ('to rob, plunder'), a rare surviving relative of the same ancient root that also gave English the word 'rob.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Bereaved is suffering the loss of a loved one.

The bereaved husband kept his wife's reading glasses on the nightstand for years after she passed.

Worked Example

Neighbors quietly take turns bringing dinner to a widow's house every evening for weeks after her husband's funeral, without ever being asked.

That state of grieving the recent loss of someone deeply loved is exactly what bereaved describes, and it's exactly why a community rallies around a family going through it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

grieving: feeling deep sorrow, especially over a death

mourning: expressing sorrow for someone's death, often through ritual or custom

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

jubilant: feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph

content: in a state of peaceful satisfaction

Where it sits · how far the sorrow turns outward — grieving → bereaved → mourning

grieving vs. bereaved: Grieving is the broader, more general word for the deep sorrow itself -- a grieving person is bereaved specifically when that sorrow follows the death of someone they loved.

mourning vs. bereaved: Mourning goes a step further than bereaved -- it often describes visibly observing grief through custom or ritual, like wearing black or holding a formal period of mourning, while bereaved simply names the state of having suffered the loss.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — be-

prefix — be-: thoroughly (an intensifier) (Old English)

root — reaved

root — reaved: to rob, plunder (a rare surviving root, also behind the English word 'rob') (Old English (reafian))

Put it together

Put it together: Bereaved combines Old English be- (an intensifying prefix, 'thoroughly') with reafian ('to rob, plunder') -- the same ancient root behind the everyday word rob -- plus the past-tense -d. To be bereaved is, at root, to have been thoroughly robbed of someone you love.

Word Choice

Bereaved is a gentle, respectful word used specifically for someone who has recently lost a loved one to death -- it's commonly paired with 'family' or 'spouse,' as in 'grief counselors work with bereaved families.'
